author_or_org: Shanna M. Kahn, John D. Hastings

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: In a study of AI-generated automation scripts, every script contained exploitable vulnerabilities.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Nine of 17 identified vulnerability classes appeared across all three models, and 14 of 17 appeared in at least two models.
claims.quote: Nine of the 17 identified vulnerability classes appeared in code from all three models, while 14 of the 17 vulnerability classes appeared in at least two models.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Weighted CVSS scores across the three AI platforms differed by less than 10%.
claims.quote: The weighted CVSS scores across platforms differed by less than 10%.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The study concludes the security risk is tied to task category rather than to a particular AI model.
claims.quote: The risk is not tied to any particular model but rather to the task category.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The paper argues organizations should ask whether LLM-generated automation code should be deployed without review, not which tool to trust.
claims.quote: Organizations should therefore ask not which tool to trust, but instead whether LLM-generated automation code should be deployed without review.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: LLM-based coding tools can let non-expert users generate routine automation scripts that enter enterprise workflows without meaningful security review.
claims.quote: LLM-based coding tools enable non-expert users to generate routine automation scripts that may enter enterprise workflows without meaningful security review.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: In the study, Claude Code performed a standardized vulnerability review of the generated code.
claims.quote: Claude Code performed a standardized vulnerability review.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Identified vulnerabilities were scored with CVSS v3.1 and mapped to OWASP Top 10:2021 and MITRE ATT&CK.
claims.quote: Each identified vulnerability was scored using CVSS v3.1 and mapped to the OWASP Top 10:2021 and the MITRE ATT&CK frameworks.
